criteria: Off by default; the person turns it on and picks one of these combinations (user decision D10, BUR-005). The first one is preselected.
No Windows key: Windows keeps Win combinations for itself and adds new ones in updates.
Ctrl+Alt never goes with a letter, a digit or a symbol: on Spanish, Latin American and many other layouts Ctrl+Alt acts as AltGr and types characters such as @, # or the euro sign.

None of the combinations that Windows or Remote Desktop handle themselves: Ctrl+Alt+Delete, Ctrl+Shift+Esc, Ctrl+Alt+Home, Ctrl+Alt+End, Ctrl+Alt+Pause and Ctrl+Alt with the arrows; and not Ctrl+Alt+F12, which some graphics drivers take.
None of the Ctrl+Alt function keys that Office uses: F1 and F2 in Word, F5 and F9 in Excel; and never Ctrl+Shift+M, Mute in Teams (BUR-005).
Never a combination of blocked-combos.json or one that the seed, the library or a template sends (GlobalHotkeyCatalogTests).
Another app may already hold the combination: then registering it fails, the product says so and the person picks another one from this list.
